title: Perf baseline dashboards + alert rules for representative suite (TTFT/TPOT/throughput/variance) with manifest links
author: Sergio Costa
description: Context: As part of the Q1'26 perf baseline + representative workload suite, we need a standard set of dashboards and alerting that (a) make baseline runs explorable, (b) make regressions actionable, and (c) are attributable via a first-class link from the panel to the run manifest + trace artifacts. This PR adds a versioned dashboard bundle and alert rules aimed at baseline runs + perf-canary outputs. What’s included: 1) Grafana dashboards (folder: "Perf Baselines") with panels for TTFT/TPOT percentiles, throughput, saturation proxies, and variance/noise views. 2) Alert rules for baseline regressions (non-paging by default) and canary gating signals (paging for release-branch gating only) with routing to the right channels/oncall. 3) Standard run label/templating conventions aligned with ADR-0172 (model, model_family, workload_id, region, sku, runtime_git_sha, scheduler_profile, kernel_profile, cache_mode, run_id). 4) Panel links: dashboard → run manifest (JSON) → trace bundle (if present). Links are built from run_id + artifact_base_url labels so we don’t have to hardcode per-environment paths. 5) A small metrics dictionary excerpt in-repo to keep dashboards stable while the full dictionary draft is iterated in Drive. Dashboards: - "Perf Baseline — Overview": top-line TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99 and throughput for the selected run cohort; quick filters for region/SKU/model/workload/cache_mode; includes a "cold vs warm" compare row. - "Perf Baseline — Latency detail": TTFT and TPOT with per-stage breakdown (client boundary vs server boundary where available), plus queue_wait_ms and batch_assembly_ms panels when the runtime emits them. - "Perf Baseline — Throughput & saturation": tokens/s, req/s (embeddings), GPU utilization (if present), batch size distribution, and a "saturation heuristics" row (queue depth, shed counters, backpressure). - "Perf Baseline — Variance": run-to-run variability panels (median absolute deviation + coefficient of variation) and a "noise budget" view to help separate regressions from fleet variability; includes warmup window visualization based on run_phase label. - "Perf Baseline — Regression compare": diff view against a selected baseline anchor (baseline_run_id) with percent deltas for p95/p99 TTFT/TPOT and throughput; flags when deltas exceed configured thresholds. Alerts: - perf_baseline_regression_warning: triggers when p99 TTFT or p99 TPOT regresses > 5% vs baseline anchor for a given (model, workload, region, sku, cache_mode) cohort, sustained over N=5 samples (configurable). Routes to #eng-runtime-perf-triage and tags the cohort in the alert annotations. - perf_baseline_variance_spike: triggers when variance (CV) exceeds threshold, indicating fleet instability; routes to #eng-sre-benchmark-fleet (non-paging). - perf_canary_gating_failure: only enabled for release branches (via label enable_gating=true); pages runtime oncall if p99 TTFT/TPOT regresses beyond gating thresholds for required cohorts. Notes on measurement boundaries: Dashboards assume TTFT/TPOT are server-side timings emitted by the benchmark harness/runtime instrumentation (not client wall-clock). We still show "first-token-on-wire" when present, but it’s not used for gating alerts. Manifest/trace linkouts: Panel links use a templated URL: ${artifact_base_url}/runs/${run_id}/manifest.json and ${artifact_base_url}/runs/${run_id}/traces/ (the trace link is conditional; shows as "Trace artifacts" with a warning when the label trace_available=false). Rollout plan: Merge behind folder-level RBAC (Engineering only). Alerts ship in disabled-by-default state for 48h dry run in staging; then enable warning alerts in prod; gating/paging remains controlled via enable_gating label and release branch policy. Testing: Validated dashboard JSON imports cleanly on grafana-staging and prod sandbox. Verified alert expressions against 2 historical baseline runs (chat_streaming and long_prefill) and confirmed annotation links resolve to manifest artifacts from benchmark-lab uploads. Screenshots: Attached in PR comments (overview + variance panel examples).

review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we align label keys with ADR-0172 exactly? Right now I see modelFamily in a couple panels. Also please ensure we don’t gate on first-token-on-wire since that includes client effects.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated panels to use model_family everywhere and added a note in the dashboard description about server-side TTFT/TPOT vs first-token-on-wire. Alerts only reference server-side series.
Aisha Bello: For variance alerts, can we make routing non-paging and land it in the benchmark fleet channel? Also add an annotation that suggests checking GPU clock locking / placement variance.
Sergio Costa (author): Done. variance_spike routes to #eng-sre-benchmark-fleet and includes a runbook link + annotation hints (clock locking, warmup, placement).
Sean Gallagher: Please gate paging alert activation behind an enable_gating label or a release-branch selector; we don’t want this paging mainline nightly until thresholds are stable.
Sergio Costa (author): Added enable_gating label requirement + documented enablement. Default is disabled. Paging only happens when enable_gating=true.
Rina Kobayashi: Manifest linkouts look good. Can we also include run_id + runtime_git_sha in the alert title so it’s searchable in Slack? We’ve been struggling to correlate to artifacts quickly.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated alert title + added annotations for run_id/runtime_git_sha and direct manifest link.
Allison Grant: Approving pending one change: please add a minimal recording rule to stabilize panel queries (reduce cardinality impact).
Sergio Costa (author): Added perf-suite recording rules for p50/p95/p99 TTFT/TPOT and throughput by cohort. Re-ran validation.
release_notes: Internal: Added Perf Baselines Grafana dashboards (TTFT/TPOT/throughput/variance) and baseline regression alert rules with run manifest + trace linkouts; paging is disabled by default and can be enabled for release gating via enable_gating=true.
